headline: 47 killed as Israel continues attacks in Lebanon despite ceasefire
summary: The escalation comes as a fragile Iran-US peace memorandum is thrown into uncertainty after scheduled talks in Switzerland were postponed.
details: At least 47 people were killed and 97 injured in Israeli airstrikes across southern Lebanon and the Beqaa Valley within a single day, according to the Lebanese Ministry of Health.
The attacks occurred despite a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hezbollah, with some strikes continuing even after a new ceasefire was announced on Friday afternoon.
The violence has cast a shadow over a peace memorandum signed by US President Donald Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, as scheduled talks in Switzerland were postponed.
A key condition of the Iran-US memorandum was that Israel would stop its attacks in Lebanon. Iran has warned that Israel will face consequences for violating this condition.
The White House confirmed that US Vice President JD Vance did not travel to Switzerland for the talks, and the Swiss Foreign Ministry stated that the the meeting did not take place.
Despite the diplomatic tension, shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has increased, with 25 ships passing through on Thursday, the highest number since April 18.

Israel's National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir has called for Lebanon to be 'burned,' further escalating the rhetoric and Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the Israeli group a 'threat to mankind.'
Four Israeli soldiers were also reported killed during clashes with Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.
caption:
47 killed in a single day. Israel continues its strikes in Lebanon, threatening a fragile peace deal between the US and Iran.

At least 47 people were killed and 97 injured in Israeli airstrikes across southern Lebanon and the Beqaa Valley within a single day, according to the Lebanese Ministry of Health.

The attacks occurred despite a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hezbollah, with some strikes continuing even after a new ceasefire was announced on Friday afternoon.

The violence has cast a shadow over a peace memorandum signed by US President Donald Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, as scheduled talks in Switzerland were postponed.

A key condition of the Iran-US memorandum was that Israel would stop its attacks in Lebanon. Iran has warned that Israel will face consequences for violating this condition.

The White House confirmed that US Vice President JD Vance did not travel to Switzerland for the talks, and the Swiss Foreign Ministry stated that the the meeting did not take place.

Despite the diplomatic tension, shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has increased, with 25 ships passing through on Thursday, the highest number since April 18.

Israel's National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir has called for Lebanon to be 'burned,' further escalating the rhetoric and Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the Israeli group a 'threat to mankind.'

Four Israeli soldiers were also reported killed during clashes with Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.

headline: 9-hour power outages planned for Saturday in several areas
summary: Certain regions of Bangladesh will face prolonged electricity cuts on Saturday to facilitate maintenance work.
details: Several areas across the country are set to experience power outages lasting up to 9 hours this Saturday.
The outages are scheduled as part of routine maintenance and system upgrades to ensure long-term stability of the power grid.
Residents in the affected regions are advised to make necessary preparations for the prolonged lack of electricity.
Local power distribution companies are managing the schedule to minimize disruption to essential services.
